result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 demonstrates strong anti-stress properties including tolerance to high temperature, strong acids (pH 2.0), bile salts, and simulated gastrointestinal fluids, with characteristic growth kinetics entering logarithmic phase after 2 hours and reaching plateau after 10 hours.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the work as providing 'convincing evidence' and note it is 'an extensive study on the probiotic properties' of the strain. The anti-stress and tolerance characteristics are part of the foundational characterization that reviewers accept without specific critique.

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 shows sensitivity to most antibiotics tested, with only polymyxin B having small inhibition zones (<15 mm), while being extremely sensitive to β-lactams, tetracyclines, and quinolones (inhibition zones >30 mm for ampicillin, meropenem, minocycline, ofloxacin, and trimethoprim), indicating the strain is not antibiotic resistant.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this as part of the 'extensive study' and safety characterization. The antibiotic susceptibility data is presented as descriptive information that reviewers do not challenge, fitting within the accepted probiotic characterization framework.

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against multiple pathogenic bacteria including E. coli, Salmonella, S. aureus, C. perfringens, S. suis, P. multocida, and A. pleuropneumoniae, with inhibition zones mostly above 15 mm, and suppresses S. Typhimurium growth in a dose-dependent manner in vitro.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state the work provides 'convincing evidence that B. velezensis limits the growth of Salmonella typhimurium in lab culture and in mice.' The in vitro antibacterial activity is accepted as part of the demonstrated probiotic effects.

result: Whole genome sequencing reveals B. velezensis HBXN2020 has a circular chromosome of 3,929,792 bp with 46.5% GC content, containing 3,744 protein-coding genes, 86 tRNA genes, 27 rRNA genes, and 13 secondary metabolite synthesis gene clusters including Fengycin and Difficidin, with phylogenetic and ANI analysis (>97% ANIb) confirming species identification.
evaluation: Reviewers note the study includes 'released genome sequence' as part of the investigation. The genomic characterization is presented as descriptive data that reviewers accept without challenge, though they note the results are 'descriptive without mechanistic insight.'

result: Safety evaluation in mice shows B. velezensis HBXN2020 administered at doses of 1×10^7, 1×10^8, and 1×10^9 CFU for 14 days causes no adverse effects, with no significant changes in body weight, inflammatory cytokines (Tnfa, Il1b, Il6, Il10), blood parameters (RBC, MCV, MCH, HGB, WBC, PLT, HCT, MCHC), serum biochemistry (ALT, AST, ALB, TBIL, CREA, BUN), or histology of colon and major organs, with slight increases in barrier proteins Tjp1 and Ocln.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study addresses 'in vivo safety issue' as part of the extensive investigation. The safety data is accepted without specific critique, supporting the conclusion that the strain 'is safe to use and has no negative side effects in mice.'

result: Therapeutic administration of B. velezensis HBXN2020 spores after S. Typhimurium infection significantly reduces bacterial loads in feces (0.12-1.18 log reduction), ileum (1.14 log), cecum (1.06 log), and colon (1.69 log), decreases disease activity index (DAI) scores (p<0.01) and weight loss (p<0.05), and prevents colon shortening (p<0.05), with effects comparable to ciprofloxacin treatment.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state the work provides 'convincing evidence that B. velezensis limits the growth of Salmonella typhimurium in lab culture and in mice.' The therapeutic efficacy data demonstrating reduced bacterial loads and clinical improvement is accepted as a key finding.

result: Histological analysis shows B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment protects colonic tissue architecture, with control and HBXN2020-only groups showing intact epithelial cells and crypt structure, while STm+PBS group exhibits significant damage (epithelial erosion, crypt destruction, inflammatory infiltration), and B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment reduces this histological damage.
evaluation: Reviewers note the study demonstrates 'protection against Salmonella infection in a murine model' with evidence of reduced 'histological damage.' The histological findings support the therapeutic efficacy claims that reviewers find convincing.

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment modulates inflammatory cytokine expression in infected mice, significantly decreasing pro-inflammatory markers Tnfa (p<0.05), Il1b (p<0.001), and Il6 (p<0.01) while increasing anti-inflammatory Il10 compared to STm+PBS group, whereas ciprofloxacin fails to reduce Il6 and drastically reduces Il10.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge 'beneficial effects on the microbiota' and protection against infection as demonstrated findings. The cytokine modulation data is accepted as part of the mechanism by which the probiotic provides protection, though reviewers note the work lacks 'mechanistic understanding.'

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment maintains intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating tight junction proteins (Tjp1, Ocln, Cldn1) and mucin (Muc2) expression that are reduced by S. Typhimurium infection, with STm+HBXN2020 group showing significantly elevated barrier protein transcription (p<0.001 for Tjp1, p<0.05 for Ocln, p<0.001 for Cldn1) and dramatically increased Muc2 compared to STm+PBS group.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the demonstration of 'beneficial effects' and protection. The barrier protein data is presented as part of the mechanism of protection, though reviewers note the overall work is 'descriptive without mechanistic insight,' suggesting acceptance of the data but desire for deeper mechanistic understanding.

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 supplementation improves colonic microbiota stability, with STm+HBXN2020 group showing higher alpha diversity (Sobs, Chao, Shannon, Simpson indexes) than STm+PBS group, and PCA analysis revealing STm+HBXN2020 microbiota composition clusters closer to control group (R²=0.1616, p=0.006) rather than STm+PBS group.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly note 'convincing evidence' of 'beneficial effects on the microbiota.' The microbiota stability and diversity data is accepted as a key finding demonstrating the probiotic's beneficial effects on gut microbial communities.

result: B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment modulates gut microbiota composition by significantly increasing beneficial bacteria Lactobacillus (p<0.05) and Akkermansia while reducing harmful bacteria (Enterococcus, Salmonella, Bacteroides, Alloprevotella, Escherichia-Shigella) compared to STm+PBS group, with ciprofloxacin treatment showing significantly lower Lactobacillus and Akkermansia abundance than B. velezensis HBXN2020 treatment, suggesting antibiotics interfere with beneficial bacteria recovery.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state the work provides 'convincing evidence' of 'beneficial effects on the microbiota.' The specific changes in beneficial and harmful bacteria are accepted as key findings, with the comparison to ciprofloxacin adding to the evidence of probiotic advantages.

result: Prophylactic administration of B. velezensis HBXN2020 spores before S. Typhimurium infection significantly reduces weight loss (p<0.01), DAI scores (p<0.001), prevents colon shortening, and decreases STm colonization in feces, ileum, cecum, and colon compared to PBS+STm group.
evaluation: Reviewers note the study demonstrates protection 'as a curative or preventive measure' and provides 'convincing evidence' of efficacy. The prophylactic efficacy data is accepted as demonstrating the probiotic's preventive potential against Salmonella infection.

result: Prophylactic B. velezensis HBXN2020 suppresses STm-induced intestinal epithelial loss, inflammatory infiltration, and colonic mucosa damage, while prophylactic ciprofloxacin fails to inhibit colonic epithelial cell loss.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the demonstration of protective effects in the prophylactic model. The histological evidence showing superior protection compared to ciprofloxacin is accepted as part of the overall finding of probiotic efficacy.

result: Prophylactic B. velezensis HBXN2020 attenuates inflammatory cytokines (Tnfa p<0.001, Il1b p<0.001, Il6 p<0.001) and increases Il10 (p<0.05), while significantly increasing barrier proteins (Tjp1 p<0.001, Ocln p<0.001, Cldn1 p<0.05, Muc2 p<0.001) compared to PBS+STm group, with CIP+STm showing significantly lower Tjp1, Ocln, and Muc2 than HBXN2020+STm group.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the prophylactic efficacy findings as part of the 'convincing evidence' of protection. The cytokine and barrier protein data in the prophylactic model parallels the therapeutic findings and is accepted without specific critique.

result: In the prophylactic model, B. velezensis HBXN2020 supplementation maintains microbiota diversity and composition similar to control group, with PCA showing significant separation between control and PBS+STm groups (R²=0.3186, p=0.014) but HBXN2020+STm clustering with control, and significantly increases Lactobacillus and Akkermansia (SCFA-producing bacteria) while PBS+STm shows lower Lactobacillus/Akkermansia and higher Alistipes, Bacteroides, Escherichia-Shigella, Enterococcus, and Alloprevotella.
evaluation: Reviewers note 'convincing evidence' of 'beneficial effects on the microbiota' in both therapeutic and prophylactic contexts. The prophylactic microbiota data is accepted as demonstrating the probiotic's ability to prevent infection-induced dysbiosis.

result: Overall, B. velezensis HBXN2020 improves intestinal microbiota stability and barrier integrity while reducing inflammation to help prevent or treat S. Typhimurium infection, with the probiotic-mediated microbial communities (especially Lactobacillus and Akkermansia) playing a crucial role in alleviating infection development, representing a novel option for preventing Salmonella infections.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state the work provides 'convincing evidence' of protection and 'beneficial effects on the microbiota,' and note the work 'will be of interest to infectious disease researchers.' However, reviewers also note the results are 'descriptive without mechanistic insight,' indicating acceptance of the findings but recognition that deeper mechanistic understanding is lacking.
